Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York had successful surgery for his torn Achilles’ tendon, his spokesman said on Friday afternoon.
He is back at his official residence at Gracie Mansion, Joe Calvello, the spokesman, said in a text message.

“The Mayor is expected to make a full recovery,” he said.

Mr. Mamdani injured his Achilles’ tendon on Nov. 19, during an evening soccer match against members of the City Hall press corps on an indoor pitch in Lower Manhattan.
“I forgot that I was 35,” Mr. Mamdani said the day after the match, after showing up to an unrelated news conference with an orthopedic boot and crutches. “And soon after, I tore my Achilles.”

The mayor’s team won the match, and Mr. Mamdani added that he had scored a goal before the injury.
The surgery was to be Mr. Mamdani’s first operation, and he had admitted that he was “scared.” The operation began at 11:33 a.m. on Friday and concluded at 12:42 p.m., Mr. Calvello said.
Both of Mr. Mamdani’s immediate predecessors underwent medical procedures that temporarily incapacitated them. Mr. Mamdani’s immediate predecessor, Eric Adams, had a colonoscopy. Bill de Blasio had surgery for a hernia and then a knee operation. His spokeswoman at the time described the hernia as a “line-of-duty” injury.

Mamdani has since been wearing a medical boot and using crutches while going about his work, including public appearances. As for the surgery, he said Monday he was apprehensive but quipped: “I just keep telling myself: Jayson Tatum did it.”
